claim: One unauthenticated `GET //` (or `//x`) terminates the worker process. `new URL(request.url, base)` throws `ERR_INVALID_URL` outside any try, and the async `createServer` callback turns it into an unhandled rejection. This runs before the origin guard and the secret check, so any caller that can reach the port can do it: a tunnel, the LAN when the host is 0.0.0.0, or a web page's no-cors `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:8644//")` (the browser vector is INFERRED). Every in-flight run dies and is marked failed on the next boot.
fix: Parse the URL in a try that returns 400, and wrap the whole request callback in a catch-all that answers 500 and never rethrows; add a router test that sends `//`. The open PR #111 (respawn a dead reused `:8644` worker in `scripts/start-discovery-worker-local.mjs`) limits the downtime but does not fix the crash or save in-flight runs.

claim: An async run can get stuck non-terminal forever. The next boot then flips a completed run to `failed`. The same pattern exists in async ingest.

It writes `exploit_outcomes` (never read: `listExploitOutcomes` has no caller) and `role_families` (read only by the planner, which is never invoked). `intentKey` is `run:${runId}`, so intent coverage can never match a later run. Each outcome row is attributed to the first lead's company. Only dead links loop back.
fix: Choose one: (a) write company/surface records from successful ATS detections, use a stable intent hash and feed exploit outcomes into frontier `priorAcceptedYield`; or (b) drop the unread tables and facades

claim: LLM calls run in the wrong order. The AI matcher (≤12 calls) runs before the deterministic profile pre-filter: 12 calls were spent on listings the pre-filter then rejected. claim: Cleanup holds every write until the full serial loop ends. The installed scheduler SIGTERMs at 45 min (about 180 rows at the 15 s timeout), so a big Sheet persists zero updates and repeats the same fetches every night.

claim: PIPE-06: four expiry writers disagree. claim: APPLY-01 persistence: the live v2 Applied flow collects applied date, source, receipt note and follow-up date, then throws them away. `updateJobStatus` writes today's date and nothing else.

claim: Half-written batches: (1) a transient 503 on the update phase aborts the append of brand-new leads, with `partialResult` null and no retry. (2) An append that commits but loses its response throws a plain TypeError, so the run is marked failed although the rows were written. A retry is idempotent by URL.
fix: Run the append even when the update fails (both are independent), retry each with backoff on 429/5xx, and classify fetch errors on append as `SheetWriteError{phase:"append", uncertain:true}`.
